notes.text: Then Paul standing in the midst of the Areopagus — An ample theatre; said - Giving them a lecture of natural divinity, with admirable wisdom, acuteness, fulness, and courtesy. They inquire after new things: Paul in his divinely philosophical discourse, begins with the first, and goes on to the last things, both which were new things to them. He points out the origin and the end of all things, concerning which they had so many disputes, and equally refutes both the Epicurean and Stoic. I perceive - With what clearness and freedom does he speak! Paul against Athens!

I found an altar — Some suppose this was set up by Socrates, to express in a covert way his devotion to the only true God, while he derided the plurality of the heathen gods, for which he was condemned to death: and others, that whoever erected this altar, did it in honour to the God of Israel, of whom there was no image, and whose name Jehovah was never made known to the idolatrous Gentiles. Him proclaim I unto you - Thus he fixes the wandering attention of these blind philosophers; proclaiming to them an unknown, and yet not a new God.
God who made the world — Thus is demonstrated even to reason, the one true, good God; absolutely different from the creatures, from every part of the visible creation.

Neither is he served as though he needed any thing — or person - The Greek word equally takes in both. To all - That live and breathe;-in him we live; and breathe - In him we move. By breathing life is continued. I breathe this moment: the next is not in my power: and all things - For in him we are. So exactly do the parts of this discourse answer each other.

He hath made of one blood the whole nation of men — By this expression the apostle showed them in the most unaffected manner, that though he was a Jew, be was not enslaved to any narrow views, but looked on all mankind as his brethren: having determined the times - That it is God who gave men the earth to inhabit, Paul proves from the order of times and places, showing the highest wisdom of the Disposer, superior to all human counsels. And the bounds of their habitation - By mountains, seas, rivers, and the like.

If haply — The way is open; God is ready to be found. But he will lay no force upon man; they might feel after him - This is in the midst between seeking and finding. Feeling being the lowest and grossest of all our senses, is fitly applied to the low knowledge of God; though he be not far from every one of us - We need not go far to seek or find him. He is very near us; in us. It is only perverse reason which thinks he is afar off.

In him — Not in ourselves, we live, and move, and have our being - This denotes his necessary, intimate, and most efficacious presence. No words can better express the continual and necessary dependence of all created beings, in their existence and all their operations, on the first and almighty cause, which the truest philosophy as well as divinity teaches. As certain also of your own poets have said - Aratus, whose words these are, was an Athenian, who lived almost three hundred years before this time. They are likewise to be found, with the alteration of one letter only, in the hymn of Cleanthes to Jupiter or the supreme being, one of the purest and finest pieces of natural religion in the whole world of Pagan antiquity.

We ought not to think — A tender expression especially in the first per son plural. As if he had said, Can God himself be a less noble being than we who are his offspring? Nor does he only here deny, that these are like God, but that they have any analogy to him at all, so as to be capable of representing him.

The times of ignorance — What! does he object ignorance to the knowing Athenians? Yes, and they acknowledge it by this very altar. God overlooked - As one paraphrases, "The beams of his eye did in a manner shoot over it." He did not appear to take notice of them, by sending express messages to them as he did to the Jews. But now - This day, this hour, saith Paul, puts an end to the Divine forbearance, and brings either greater mercy or punishment. Now he commandeth all men everywhere to repent - There is a dignity and grandeur in this expression, becoming an ambassador from the King of heaven. And this universal demand of repentance declared universal guilt in the strongest manner, and admirably confronted the pride of the haughtiest Stoic of them all. At the same time it bore down the idle plea of fatality. For how could anyone repent of doing what he could not but have done?

He hath appointed a day in which he will judge the world — How fitly does he speak this, in their supreme court of justice? By the man - So he speaks, suiting himself to the capacity of his hearers. Whereof he hath given assurance to all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead - God raising Jesus demonstrated hereby, that he was to be the glorious Judge of all. We are by no means to imagine that this was all which the apostle intended to have said, but the indolence of some of his hearers and the petulancy of others cut him short.

glossa.text:
*Men of Athens,* etc. *What you worship in ignorance, that I preach.* He answers to that which they had said or had put forward: *Thou bringest in certain new things,* as if he said: The new things which I bring in you have among your old ones. And this he says for persuasion, lest they refute his words as new.

*To an unknown God. ((RAB.))* That is, to the true God, whom no one knows as he is, etc., *as far as* that which is passed over in silence, or it was simply written: *To an unknown God.*

*God, who made the world.* Note the order of this disputation, because first he teaches that one God is the author of the world, of all things, in whom we live, and are moved, and are, whose offspring also we are: so that not only for light and life, but also for the kinship of race, he may be shown to be one who ought to be loved.
*Of one all the race of men.* In the Greek: *of one blood,* because blood designates the propagation of the flesh, and by the flesh man is understood.

*For in him we live. ((AUG.))* Because he works that in us, which is that *we live, are moved, and are,* etc., *as far as* because what is not of him, of whom it is said: *Of him, and by him, and in him are all things ((Rom. II))*?

*As also certain of your own poets.* To those who did not receive the prophets he speaks the testimony, not of Moses, not of Isaias, or of any of the prophets, but of their own authors, setting down a verse of Aratus, and out of their own false things, which they could not contradict, he preserves and confirms his own truth. *For his,* etc. This testimony was taken from the poet Aratus, not from the divine page, lest he should seem to bring in new things.
*Being therefore,* etc., *we ought not. ((RAB.))* Man is in the middle, having God as higher, gold from silver, with the rest of this kind as lower, which ought not to be compared to him.
*God despising. ((ID.))* That is, pardoning them as venial, and then despising, that is, judging them unworthy of his notice.
*Giving faith to all. ((ID.))* By the example of his own resurrection: or, he has appointed to judge, and afterward it is to be joined thus, giving faith to all that they shall rise again.

notes.text: Proved us — As it were in a burning furnace; and with a design to purge out our dross.
Net — Which our enemies laid for us.
To ride — To use us like slaves.
I will go — One speaks in the name of all the rest. Incense - With the fat of rams, which is no less pleasing to God than incense.

Iniquity — Any sin. In heart - If my heart had been false to God, although I might have forborne outward acts. If I had been guilty of that, by heart was set upon sin, or I desired only that which I resolved in my heart to spend upon my lusts. A prayer for Israel, ver. 1. For the conversion of the Gentiles, ver. 2-5. A prospect of glorious times, ver. 6, 7. To the chief musician on Neginoth, A psalm or song.

glossa.text: *Bless ye.* ((CAS.)) Diapsalma. He admonishes the Gentiles to bless God, who, although he tries them by tribulations, yet leads them to the kingdom; for these things seem to stand in the way of the promised resurrection. *Make ye heard.* ((AUG.)) Openly, so that he who loves God loves his neighbour also. *The voice of his praise.* Which the Father speaks of the Son: *This is my Son.*

*Who hath set my soul. ((Ibid.))* Here he enumerates for what causes he ought to be preached.

 *For thou hast proved us.* [n: (AUG.)] Thou hast not given us over unto commotion. Because thou hast proved us, thou hast not cast us headlong, thou hast proved us by adversities, by the fire of charity, which does not suffer us to feel torments, or, thou hast tried us by the fire of tribulation, etc.
*A snare.* ((AUG.)) Not one that deceives, but one that proves. *We have passed over.* ((CAS.; AUG.)) Thou all these things, and we, etc., *as far as* this happens to us in temptations.

*I will go in.* ((CAS.)) Behold what good things against the evils that went before, that he may strengthen us. *In holocausts.* That is, that I may offer myself to thy sight, etc., *as far as* but he withdrew that which is dearer, himself.

*They have distinguished.* ((AUG.)) He distinguishes who says that he himself is nothing, and God all things; and that he himself has need of God, not God of him. *And my mouth hath spoken.* Whom before all men I have declared to prevail above all other vows in my tribulation, not overcome by tribulation.

*Marrowy holocausts.* Myself, with the marrow of inmost love. *With the burnt offering of rams. ((Ibid.))* Or, with *the burnt offering,* which is prayer; and with *rams,* because the leaders of the flock pray most of all for the flock. *With the burnt offering.* ((HIER., AUG.)) With the prayer of the Apostles, because that pleases God which is done by their tradition. Or with the burning and destruction of brutishness and of resistance. Oxen; stiffness of neck; *with he-goats,* wantonness; these vices being slain in me. *I will offer thee oxen.* ((AUG.)) If those who thresh are offered, yet they do not remain sinners: but healed through penance they are offered; and they not by themselves, but rather joined to the oxen, because they have made themselves friends of the mammon of iniquity.

*Come ye, hear.* Diapsalma. All things now being set forth, he again admonishes not so much the untaught, but the devout, that by the example of his own deliverance they may trust the more in the Lord: blessing him for the hearing of his prayer. So do I, and O ye Gentiles, *come ye.*

*To him I have cried with my mouth.* ((CAS.)) He sets forth how great things he did for his own soul, subjoining: *To him,* etc. This he did for my soul, that I should cry to him, while the Gentiles cried to idols: and what I speak without I have within, and not iniquity, because thus is the purity of prayer, it is heard. *I have cried and exalted in my heart.* ((AUG.)) That is, I have preached him publicly, and confessed him in secret. What I have in the mouth, this I have in the heart also: yet *I will offer marrowy holocausts.* By these two the Christian is made perfect.
*Mine.* That is a man's own which is not perverse; he sets it forth with reason, that they may learn to labour first before they seek the reward.
*My prayer,* etc. These two are joined together; if prayer is not suspended, neither is mercy deferred.

notes.text: Who is he that will harm you — None can.
But if ye should suffer — This is no harm to you, but a good. Fear ye not their fear - The very words of the Septuagint, Isaiah viii, 12, 13. Let not that fear be in you which the wicked feel.

But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts — Have an holy fear, and a full trust in his wise providence. The hope - Of eternal life. With meekness - For anger would hurt your cause as well as your soul. And fear - A filial fear of offending God, and a jealousy over yourselves, lest ye speak amiss.

Having a good conscience — So much the more beware of anger, to which the very consciousness of your innocence may betray you. Join with a good conscience meekness and fear, and you obtain a complete victory. Your good conversation in Christ - That is, which flows from faith in him.
It is infinitely better, if it be the will of God, ye should suffer. His permissive will appears from his providence.

For — This is undoubtedly best, whereby we are most conformed to Christ. Now Christ suffered once - To suffer no more. For sins - Not his own, but ours. The just for the unjust - The word signifies, not only them who have wronged their neighbours, but those who have transgressed any of the commands of God; as the preceding word, just, denotes a person who has fulfilled, not barely social duties, but all kind of righteousness. That he might bring us to God - Now to his gracious favour, hereafter to his blissful presence, by the same steps of suffering and of glory. Being put to death in the flesh - As man. But raised to life by the Spirit - Both by his own divine power, and by the power of the Holy Ghost.

By which Spirit he preached — Through the ministry of Noah. To the spirits in prison - The unholy men before the flood, who were then reserved by the justice of God, as in a prison, till he executed the sentence upon them all; and are now also reserved to the judgment of the great day.
When the longsuffering of God waited — For an hundred and twenty years; all the time the ark was preparing: during which Noah warned them all to flee from the wrath to come.

The antitype whereof — The thing typified by the ark, even baptism, now saveth us - That is, through the water of baptism we are saved from the sin which overwhelms the world as a flood: not, indeed, the bare outward sign, but the inward grace; a divine consciousness that both our persons and our actions are accepted through him who died and rose again for us.
Angels and authorities and powers — That is, all orders both of angels and men.

glossa.text: *And who is he. ((BEDA.))* Therefore you are bound *debitis*; read *debetis*, "you ought" to turn aside from evil and to do good, because no one can draw you back from the good, nor from the crown, if you shall have willed to persist, nay rather they profit you while they wish to harm.
*But the fear.* In the future you shall be blessed, but in the present *fear ye not their fear,* that is, those things in them which can seem to be feared, such as royal power, and the like.

*But the Lord.* The holiness of Christ; behold with the inmost affection of the heart of how incomprehensible a glory it is, and so sanctify Christ himself in you, that he depart not from the memory, not from the love. He who does not consider this holiness fails before the snares of the enemy. *To every one that asketh.* To him that is willing to receive reasonable moneys on loan, let us not refuse. Whence Paul: *Walk in wisdom for the sake of them that are without, knowing how it behoveth to answer every one.* For they that are without, that is, they that are not yet faithful, wish to know something of the hope which is in you. He therefore who presides over the ecclesiastical teaching, let him teach those that are patient, let him stop the mouths of those that resist.
*But with modesty.* In the very knowledge of doctrine he admonishes that the manner of teaching be observed, that humility may be shown both in living and in speaking.
*It is better. ((BEDA.))* So ought you to bear with your slanderers and to confound them, etc., *as far as* he is removed and is prepared for eternal vengeance.

*He might offer to God. ((ID.))* Because even then, if any had been willing to believe at the preaching of the Lord (which they set forth through the life of the faithful), he rejoiced to offer them to God the Father. But if any disparaged the good as though they were evildoers, at the imminence of the flood they were confounded.

*In prison. ((ID.))* They who have their sense darkened with shadows are rightly said to be shut up in prison even in this life, and in this inward prison of the mind they are weighed down by unjust works, until, loosed from the flesh, they are cast into the exterior darkness of eternal damnation. The just also have a prison here, but one of tribulations, whereas the reprobate have one of vices.

*When they waited for the patience of God.* When the patience of God invited them to repentance, sparing them for the hundred years in which Noe was building the ark, by which was shown what was to come to pass in the world. They therefore did not use the patience of God unto repentance, but awaited it as though it were going to endure for ever. *Noe.* Noe is interpreted rest, and signifies Christ who gives to his faithful the rest of souls.

*When the ark was a building. ((BEDA.))* As the ark was built of planed timbers, so the Church of the gathering of faithful souls: and as, when the world was perishing, few were saved by water: so, in comparison with those that perish, small is the number of the elect, because narrow is the way which leads to life, and few there are that find it.

*Whereunto you also of the like form.* Baptism makes men safe, baptism, I say, *of the like form,* that is, likened in all things to that ark, because whatsoever is there done carnally, here is done spiritually.

*Not the putting away of the flesh,* etc. I do not say that that baptism saves where there is only *a putting away of the filth of the flesh,* that is, where the flesh only is washed outwardly (which the heretics had), but where there is *the examination of a pure conscience,* that is, where a good conscience of him that is to be baptized is asked and required by the baptizer: because such a baptism saves, another kills; the examination has been made tending unto God, that through a good conscience he may be made one with God.

*Swallowing up death. ((BEDA.))* What we swallow down, we bring it about that, taken into our bodies, it nowhere appears: so the Lord utterly consumed death, that it might avail nothing against him, and, the appearance of a true body remaining, the stain of the ancient frailty was absent. Which is promised to us also, whence he adds, *that we also might be made heirs of eternal life. The angels being made subject to him.* We do not doubt that the angels were always subject to the Son of God, but he here makes mention of the subjection for this reason, that he might show the assumed humanity so exalted in the resurrection that it is preferred before every power of angelic dignity. Whence, *thou hast subjected all things under his feet ((Psal. VIII))*.

notes.text: If ye love me, keep my commandments — Immediately after faith he exhorts to love and good works.

And I will ask the Father — The 21st verse, ver. 21, shows the connection between this and the preceding verses. And he will give you another Comforter - The Greek word signifies also an advocate, instructer, or encourager. Another - For Christ himself was one. To remain with you forever - With you, and your followers in faith, to the end of the world.

The Spirit of truth — Who has, reveals, testifies, and defends the truth as it is in Jesus. Whom the world - All who do not love or fear God, cannot receive, because it seeth him not - Having no spiritual senses, no internal eye to discern him; nor consequently knoweth him. He shall be in you - As a constant guest. Your bodies and souls shall be temples of the Holy Ghost dwelling in you.

I will not leave you orphans — A word that is elegantly applied to those who have lost any dear friend. I come to you - What was certainly and speedily to be, our Lord speaks of as if it were already.

But ye see me — That is, ye shall certainly see me. Because I live, ye shall live also - Because I am the living One in my Divine nature, and shall rise again in my human nature, and live for ever in heaven: therefore ye shall live the life of faith and love on earth, and hereafter the life of glory.
At that day — When ye see me after my resurrection; but more eminently at the day of pentecost.
He that hath my commandments — Written in his heart. I will manifest myself to him - More abundantly.

glossa.text: *If you love me.* How does he admonish them to love and to keep the commandments, that they may receive the Spirit, whom unless they have they cannot love and keep? But what they had in less measure, secretly, they were to receive more abundantly, openly, so that what they had might become known to them.

*And I will ask the Father. ((THEOPH.))* I will ask, that is, I will beseech the Father, and he will send you another Paraclete, etc., *as far as* that the Paraclete Spirit and his condescending grace may wholly come upon them, he says to them: *I will ask the Father.*

*Because it seeth him not,* etc. The lovers of the world have not spiritual eyes wherewith they might see the Holy Spirit. Nor indeed can they see him with carnal eyes, because the Holy Spirit did not appear clothed in humanity. *And in you.* He shall be in you; he shall not abide in order to be, because to be somewhere is prior to abiding. Let no one therefore think that he so abides as a guest visibly with another; but in them he can be known, not by others.
*I will not leave.* The Spirit shall not be given in my stead in such a way that I too am not with you. Orphani is Greek, pupilli is Latin.

*Yet a little while, and the world.* But the world, which now sees with the eyes of the flesh, after a little while shall not see, because when raised again he did not show himself to them; but the whole time is little, and when it is ended the impious man shall be taken away, that he may not see the glory of God, which the just shall see. *Because I live, and you shall live.* He uses the present, because his resurrection is soon to be. Of those he uses the future, whose resurrection is to be at the end.
*And you in me, and I in you.* This is so now, and is known after a fashion through faith; but then it shall be known through sight, when this conjunction shall be perfected which is now begun.

*He that hath,* etc. Not only you apostles shall live and shall know, but also whosoever has [them] in memory and keeps [them] in life. Or, he has by doing, keeps by persevering. Or he who has [them] in his discourses keeps [them] in his manners. Or, he has by hearing, keeps by doing. *And I will love him.* To this end will I love him, that I may manifest [myself], because even now he loves, but not to this end, but rather that we may believe and keep the commandments, that we may deserve what we may afterwards receive. *And I will manifest to him.* He who has my commandment, he knows me, and this is [what stands] there: *I will manifest myself to him.* But he sets first the cause of the commandment, because he loves me; and he who loves me, my Father will love him, and because the Father [loves him], then I too will love him, and thence comes the manifestation.

hymns.title: Silent waters rocking on the morning of our birth
Baptized in water, sealed by the Spirit,
This is the Spirit's entry now
At the font we start our journey

echoes.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
echoes.note: 'The God who made the world and all things in it' is creation-monotheism rooted in the opening of Genesis; high volume and thematic coherence, the foundation of the whole sermon.

echoes.text: Thus says God Yahweh, he who created the heavens and stretched them out, he who spread out the earth and that which comes out of it, he who gives breath to its people and spirit to those who walk in it.
echoes.note: Isaiah's God who 'created the heavens... gives breath to the people upon it and spirit to those who walk in it' tightly combines both of Paul's claims: maker of the world (v.24) and giver of life and breath (v.25). Strong verbal and conceptual overlap.

echoes.text: But will God in very deed dwell on the earth? Behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens can’t contain you; how much less this house that I have built!
echoes.note: Solomon's 'heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you; how much less this house I have built' directly grounds 'does not dwell in temples made with hands.' Strong thematic coherence at the dedication of the very institution Paul relativizes.

echoes.text: Thus says Yahweh, “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool: what kind of house will you build to me? and what place shall be my rest? For all these things has my hand made, and so all these things came to be,” says Yahweh: “but to this man will I look, even to him who is poor and of a contrite spirit, and who trembles at my word.
echoes.note: 'Heaven is my throne and the earth my footstool; what house will you build for me?' is the prophetic charter for 'does not dwell in temples made with hands' and for needing nothing from human hands; quoted by Stephen in Acts 7, so recurrence in Acts is high.

echoes.text: Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
echoes.note: 'He himself gives to all life and breath' echoes God breathing the breath of life into the man; foundational creation text for the life-giver claim.

echoes.text: When the Most High gave to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the children of men, he set the bounds of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel.
echoes.note: 'When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance... he fixed the boundaries of the peoples' is the key text behind v.26, God making every nation and 'fixing the boundaries of their dwellings.' Strong verbal and conceptual coherence.

echoes.text: To whom then will you liken God? Or what likeness will you compare to him? A workman has cast an image, and the goldsmith overlays it with gold, and casts silver chains for it. He who is too impoverished for such an offering chooses a tree that will not rot. He seeks a skillful workman to set up an engraved image for him that will not be moved.
echoes.note: 'To whom will you liken God?... a craftsman casts an idol, a goldsmith overlays it with gold' directly grounds v.29, that the Divine Nature is not 'like gold, or silver, or stone, engraved by art.'

echoes.text: For verily all men by nature were but vain who had no perception of God, And from the good things that are seen they gained not power to know him that is, Neither by giving heed to the works did they recognize the architect; But either fire, or wind, or swift air, Or circling stars, or raging water, or luminaries of heaven, They thought to be gods that rule the world. And if it was through delight in their beauty that they took them to be gods, Let them […]
echoes.note: Wisdom's critique that people who admired the world's beauty failed to find its Maker, yet are 'not to be excused' because they could seek and find, closely tracks vv.24-29 (knowing the Creator from creation, seeking and finding). The deuterocanonical natural-theology bridge is the nearest analogue to the whole Areopagus argument.

echoes.text: before Yahweh; for he comes, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, the peoples with his truth.
echoes.note: 'He comes to judge the earth; he will judge the world in righteousness' is almost verbatim with v.31, that God 'will judge the world in righteousness.' High volume.

echoes.text: He will judge the world in righteousness. He will administer judgment to the peoples in uprightness.
echoes.note: 'He will judge the world in righteousness' is a near-exact verbal parallel to v.31; recurrence of this formula across the Psalter strengthens the link.

echoes.text: Let them sing before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with equity.
echoes.note: 'He comes to judge the earth; he will judge the world with righteousness' is the third near-identical parallel to v.31, confirming a fixed liturgical formula behind Paul's words.

echoes.text: for in six days Yahweh made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested the seventh day; therefore Yahweh blessed the Sabbath day, and made it holy.
echoes.note: 'made the heaven and the earth, the sea and all that is in them' is echoed in 'made the world and all things in it... Lord of heaven and earth'; recurrent creation formula.

echoes.text: who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them; who keeps truth forever;
echoes.note: 'who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them' parallels v.24's creation summary; recurrence of the formula raises confidence.

echoes.text: “But will God indeed dwell with men on the earth? Behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens can’t contain you; how much less this house which I have built!
echoes.note: Parallel to 1 Kings 8:27, the same temple-cannot-contain-God confession behind v.24.

echoes.text: I don’t rebuke you for your sacrifices. Your burnt offerings are continually before me. I have no need for a bull from your stall, nor male goats from your pens. For every animal of the forest is mine, and the livestock on a thousand hills. I know all the birds of the mountains. The wild animals of the field are mine. If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is mine, and all that is in it. Will I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of […]
echoes.note: 'If I were hungry I would not tell you, for the world and its fullness are mine' grounds v.25, that God is not 'served by human hands as though he needed anything'; strong thematic coherence with sacrificial critique.

echoes.text: in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?
echoes.note: 'In his hand is the life of every living thing and the breath of all mankind' closely matches 'gives to all life and breath.'

echoes.text: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them. God blessed them. God said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and subdue it. Have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the sky, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”
echoes.note: 'Made from one... every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth' draws on the creation and filling of the earth from the one human pair.

echoes.text: He increases the nations, and he destroys them. He enlarges the nations, and he leads them captive.
echoes.note: 'He makes nations great, and destroys them; he enlarges nations, and leads them away' parallels v.26's sovereign setting of appointed times and boundaries for peoples.

echoes.text: You have set all the boundaries of the earth. You have made summer and winter.
echoes.note: 'You have fixed all the boundaries of the earth' directly supports 'the boundaries of their dwellings' in v.26.

echoes.text: But from there you shall seek Yahweh your God, and you shall find him, when you search after him with all your heart and with all your soul.
echoes.note: 'You will seek the LORD your God and you will find him, if you search with all your heart' underlies v.27, that the nations 'should seek the Lord... and find him.'

echoes.text: Seek Yahweh while he may be found; call you on him while he is near:
echoes.note: 'Seek the LORD while he may be found' parallels v.27's seek-and-find; recurrent prophetic summons.

echoes.text: Yahweh is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.
echoes.note: 'The LORD is near to all who call on him' grounds 'he is not far from each one of us' (v.27).

echoes.text: Am I a God at hand, says Yahweh, and not a God afar off? Can any hide himself in secret places so that I shall not see him? says Yahweh. Don’t I fill heaven and earth? says Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'Am I a God near at hand... and not a God far off? Do I not fill heaven and earth?' closely supports 'not far from each one of us' and the immanence of vv.27-28.

echoes.text: Everyone who makes an engraved image is vain. The things that they delight in will not profit. Their own witnesses don’t see, nor know, that they may be disappointed. Who has fashioned a god, or molds an image that is profitable for nothing? Behold, all his fellows will be disappointed; and the workmen are mere men. Let them all be gathered together. Let them stand up. They will fear. They will be put to shame together. The blacksmith takes an ax, works […]
echoes.note: The craftsman who fashions a god from wood/metal stands behind v.29's rejection of images 'engraved by art and design of man.'

echoes.text: There you shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.
echoes.note: Idols 'the work of human hands, wood and stone, which neither see nor hear' parallels v.29's gold, silver, and stone made by human craft.

echoes.text: But miserable were they, and in dead things were their hopes, Who called them gods which are works of men’s hands, Gold and silver, wrought with careful are, and likenesses of animals, Or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand.
echoes.note: 'Miserable... who called gods the works of human hands, gold and silver fashioned with skill, and likenesses of animals, or useless stone' is verbally very close to v.29's gold, silver, and stone shaped by human art.

echoes.text: But you have mercy on all men, because you have power to do all things, And you overlookest the sins of men to the end they may repent.
echoes.note: 'You overlook the sins of men, that they may repent' parallels v.30, God 'overlooked' the times of ignorance and now commands repentance.

echoes.text: Say among the nations, “Yahweh reigns.” The world is also established. It can’t be moved. He will judge the peoples with equity.
echoes.note: 'He will judge the peoples with equity' reinforces the universal-righteous-judgment theme of v.31.

echoes.text: “Yet I have set my King on my holy hill of Zion.” I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father. Ask of me, and I will give the nations for your inheritance, the uttermost parts of the earth for your possession. You shall break them with a rod of iron. You shall dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.”
echoes.note: Judgment 'by the man whom he has ordained' evokes the installed/anointed son to whom the nations are given; coherent with the appointed agent of v.31.

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. There was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
echoes.note: Judgment of the world entrusted to 'the man' (anthropos) recalls the son of man given everlasting dominion and judgment; supports the human appointed judge of v.31.

echoes.text: You are Yahweh, even you alone. You have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their army, the earth and all things that are on it, the seas and all that is in them, and you preserve them all. The army of heaven worships you.
echoes.note: 'You made heaven... the earth and all that is on it... and you give life to them all' parallels both creation and life-giving themes; included as a recurrent OT confession.

echoes.text: He blessed him, and said, “Blessed be Abram of God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth:
echoes.note: 'Lord of heaven and earth' (v.24) echoes 'God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth'; faint title-level contact.

echoes.text: Behold, to Yahweh your God belongs heaven and the heaven of heavens, the earth, with all that is therein.
echoes.note: 'heaven and the heaven of heavens, the earth and all that is in it' supports 'Lord of heaven and earth'; recurrent title.

echoes.text: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
echoes.note: 'The breath of the Almighty gives me life' parallels v.25's life and breath; recurrent wisdom motif.

echoes.text: They fell on their faces, and said, “God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and will you be angry with all the congregation?”
echoes.note: 'God of the spirits of all flesh' supports the universal life-giver theme of v.25.

echoes.text: For thus says the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite. For I will not contend forever, neither will I be always angry; for the spirit would faint before me, and the souls who I have made.
echoes.note: The high and lofty One who nonetheless gives breath ('the breath that I have made') touches v.25; faint.

echoes.text: These are the families of the sons of Noah, by their generations, according to their nations. The nations divided from these in the earth after the flood.
echoes.note: The Table of Nations, all peoples spreading 'from one' after the flood, underlies the unity-of-nations claim in v.26.

echoes.text: God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of sky to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs to mark seasons, days, and years;
echoes.note: 'Determined appointed seasons' may glance at the luminaries set 'for seasons'; faint, since the sense here is more likely the epochs of nations.

echoes.text: You shall seek me, and find me, when you shall search for me with all your heart.
echoes.note: 'You will seek me and find me, when you seek with all your heart' parallels v.27; recurrent seek-and-find formula.

echoes.text: For what great nation is there, that has a god so near to them, as Yahweh our God is whenever we call on him?
echoes.note: 'What nation has a god so near to it as the LORD?' supports the nearness theme of v.27; faint.

echoes.text: “To whom will you liken me, and make me equal, and compare me, that we may be like? Some pour out gold from the bag, and weigh silver in the balance. They hire a goldsmith, and he makes it a god. They fall down—yes, they worship. They bear it on the shoulder, they carry it, and set it in its place, and it stands, from its place it shall not move: yes, one may cry to it, yet it can not answer, nor save him out of his trouble.
echoes.note: 'To whom will you liken me?... they hire a goldsmith who makes it into a god' parallels v.29; recurrent Isaianic idol-polemic.

echoes.text: Remember the commandments, and be not angry with your neighbor; And remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.
echoes.note: Faint contact with the call to overlook ignorance and turn; weak link to v.30.

echoes.text: For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it is good, or whether it is evil.
echoes.note: 'God will bring every deed into judgment' supports the coming-judgment theme of v.31; faint, no verbal contact.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

spans.label: Second journey
spans.note: Split with Barnabas; took Silas, picked up Timothy and Luke. Crossed into Europe at the Macedonian call — the Philippian jailer, the Areopagus, and a year and a half building the church at Corinth.

places.name: Athens
places.id: In Roman Achaia, by the apostolic period a renowned cultural centre well past its political prime. The agora, Areopagus rock, and Acropolis remained the principal sites of intellectual and civic life.

places.name: Areopagus
places.id: The rocky hill northwest of the Athenian Acropolis where the ancient council of Areopagus met. By the Roman period its judicial and supervisory role was reduced; the council still oversaw matters of religion and education, which is why a new teaching like Paul’s would naturally come before it.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: “Don’t say, ‘A conspiracy!’ concerning all about which this people say, ‘A conspiracy!’ neither fear their threats, nor be terrorized. Yahweh of Armies is who you must respect as holy. He is the one you must fear. He is the one you must dread.
echoes.note: 1 Peter 3:14-15 quotes Isaiah 8:12-13: 'Do not fear what they fear, neither be troubled (Isa 8:12), but sanctify the LORD of hosts (Isa 8:13)' — Peter christologizes it to 'sanctify the Lord [Christ] God in your hearts.' The Isaianic 'do not fear, do not be in dread, but the LORD of hosts him you shall regard as holy' becomes the charter for fearless witness under hostility. Formal quotation woven into the exhortation.

echoes.text: Depart from evil, and do good. seek peace, and pursue it.
echoes.note: 'Be zealous for / imitators of that which is good' and 'suffer for righteousness' sake' (3:13-14) continue the Psalm 34 program just quoted ('depart from evil and do good'); the do-good ethic flows directly out of the citation, a recurrence binding the pericopes.

echoes.text: He will be a sanctuary, but for both houses of Israel, he will be a trap and a snare for the inhabitants of Jerusalem. Many will stumble over it, fall, be broken, be snared, and be captured.”
echoes.note: The immediately following Isaianic 'stone of stumbling and rock of offense' (echoed in 1 Pet 2:8) suggests Peter has the whole Isaiah 8 context in view; the suffering-righteous who fear God not man inhabit that sanctuary-vs-stumbling frame. Contextual echo.

echoes.text: For the Lord Yahweh will help me; therefore I have not been confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be disappointed. He is near who justifies me; who will bring charges against me? Let us stand up together: who is my adversary? Let him come near to me. Behold, the Lord Yahweh will help me; who is he who shall condemn me? Behold, all they shall wax old as a garment, the moth shall eat them up.
echoes.note: The Servant's confident 'the Lord GOD helps me... who will declare me guilty?' parallels 3:13 'who is he who will harm you, if you become imitators of that which is good?' — vindication of the righteous sufferer. Faint, thematic.

echoes.text: When men began to multiply on the surface of the ground, and daughters were born to them, God’s sons saw that men’s daughters were beautiful, and they took any that they wanted for themselves as wives. Yahweh said, “My Spirit will not strive with man forever, because he also is flesh; so his days will be one hundred twenty years.” The Nephilim were in the earth in those days, and also after that, when God’s sons came in to men’s daughters and had children […]
echoes.note: The flood narrative is invoked typologically: 'the days of Noah while the ship was being built' (3:20). Peter reads the wickedness and judgment of the antediluvian world (Gen 6) as the backdrop against which the ark/baptism deliverance is the antitype (antitypos, 3:21). The flood's saving-through-water becomes the type fulfilled in baptism — explicitly figural.

echoes.text: Yahweh said to Noah, “Come with all of your household into the ship, for I have seen your righteousness before me in this generation. You shall take seven pairs of every clean animal with you, the male and his female. Of the animals that are not clean, take two, the male and his female. Also of the birds of the sky, seven and seven, male and female, to keep seed alive on the surface of all the earth. In seven days, I will cause it to rain on the earth for […]
echoes.note: 'Few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water' (3:20) cites the ark deliverance of Genesis 7 (Noah, his wife, three sons and their wives = eight). The salvation 'through water' is the explicit antitype of baptism in 3:21 — the flood-water that destroyed the disobedient world saves the elect remnant in the ark. Typological/figural reading of the flood as baptism.

echoes.text: Yahweh says to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool for your feet.”
echoes.note: 'Who is at the right hand of God' (3:22) cites the enthronement formula of Psalm 110:1 'Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.' The subjection of 'angels and authorities and powers' to the exalted Christ realizes the footstool-of-enemies motif. The most-cited royal psalm for Christ's exaltation.

echoes.text: God remembered Noah, all the animals, and all the livestock that were with him in the ship; and God made a wind to pass over the earth. The waters subsided. The deep’s fountains and the sky’s windows were also stopped, and the rain from the sky was restrained. The waters continually receded from the earth. After the end of one hundred fifty days the waters decreased. The ship rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on Ararat’s […]
echoes.note: God's 'waiting patiently in the days of Noah' (3:20) reflects the long patience while the ark was built and the flood receded (Gen 8); the divine forbearance toward the disobedient generation undergirds the patience motif. Recurrence within the Noah cycle.

echoes.text: Yahweh said, “My Spirit will not strive with man forever, because he also is flesh; so his days will be one hundred twenty years.”
echoes.note: 'My Spirit shall not abide in man forever... his days shall be 120 years' — the limited span of divine patience before the flood — directly informs '(God) waited patiently in the days of Noah' (3:20), the period of forbearance before judgment.

echoes.text: When men began to multiply on the surface of the ground, and daughters were born to them, God’s sons saw that men’s daughters were beautiful, and they took any that they wanted for themselves as wives. Yahweh said, “My Spirit will not strive with man forever, because he also is flesh; so his days will be one hundred twenty years.” The Nephilim were in the earth in those days, and also after that, when God’s sons came in to men’s daughters and had children […]
echoes.note: The 'sons of God' who transgressed before the flood (Gen 6:1-4) feed the Second-Temple Watchers tradition (1 Enoch) widely thought to lie behind 'the spirits in prison' to whom Christ preached (3:19). Contested: whether the spirits are fallen angels (Watchers) or the human dead of Noah's generation.

echoes.text: After the suffering of his soul, he will see the light and be satisfied. My righteous servant will justify many by the knowledge of himself; and he will bear their iniquities. Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the plunder with the strong; because he poured out his soul to death, and was numbered with the transgressors; yet he bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.
echoes.note: 'Christ also suffered for sins once, the righteous for the unrighteous' (3:18) draws on the Servant who 'bore the sin of many' and 'the righteous one, my servant, shall make many to be accounted righteous.' The vicarious righteous-for-unrighteous formula extends 1 Peter's sustained use of Isaiah 53 (cf. 2:22-25).

echoes.text: The earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence. God saw the earth, and saw that it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth. God said to Noah, “I will bring an end to all flesh, for the earth is filled with violence through them. Behold, I will destroy them and the earth.
echoes.note: The 'disobedient' spirits/generation 'who before were disobedient in the days of Noah' (3:19-20) echo the corruption and violence that filled the earth (Gen 6:11-13). Faint, depends on identifying the 'spirits in prison' with the Noahic generation.

echoes.text: Behold, my servant shall deal wisely, he shall be exalted and lifted up, and shall be very high.
echoes.note: The Servant who is 'exalted and lifted up' parallels the exaltation of the suffering-then-glorified Christ 'at the right hand of God, having gone into heaven' (3:22). Faint, part of the Isaiah 52-53 Servant arc.

echoes.text: For you will not leave my soul in Sheol, neither will you allow your holy one to see corruption.
echoes.note: 'Put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the spirit' (3:18) and Christ's descent/proclamation faintly echo the Psalm of resurrection hope ('you will not abandon my soul to Sheol'), a text early Christians applied to Christ's vindication from death. Faint, thematic.

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. There was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
echoes.note: The exaltation of the suffering one to heavenly dominion over 'angels and authorities and powers' (3:22) recalls the Son of Man given everlasting dominion and all powers subjected to him. Faint, thematic cosmic-subjection parallel.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: 'I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes' supplies the new-covenant gift of an indwelling Spirit that produces obedience, exactly the logic of 14:15-17 where loving-and-obeying flows into the Paraclete who 'will be in you.' High Coherence: the Spirit given to dwell within and to enable commandment-keeping is Ezekiel's signature promise.

echoes.text: You shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.
echoes.note: The Shema's command to 'love the LORD your God' grounds the love-of-God demanded in 14:15, now reoriented to Jesus: 'if you love me, keep my commandments.' Coherence is strong because John fuses love and obedience in the Deuteronomic manner; medium rather than high since the wording is paraphrased and reattributed to Jesus.

echoes.text: Know therefore that Yahweh your God himself is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness with them who love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations,
echoes.note: God keeps covenant 'with those who love him and keep his commandments,' the precise love+keep-commandments pairing echoed in 14:15 and 14:21. Recurrence of this formula across Deuteronomy raises Volume; the contestation is that John supplies the idiom without a citation marker.

echoes.text: and showing loving kindness to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.
echoes.note: The Decalogue promises steadfast love 'to those who love me and keep my commandments,' the foundational love-and-obey formula behind 14:15. Strong Coherence with John's repeated linkage of loving Jesus and keeping his word; medium because it is one of several overlapping Pentateuchal sources for the same idiom.

echoes.text: The Spirit of Yahweh will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'The Spirit of the LORD shall rest on him, the Spirit of wisdom... and of knowledge' anchors the messianic 'Spirit of truth' the Father gives in 14:17. Coherence is good because Isaiah's endowing Spirit is a Spirit of knowledge/truth resting permanently; medium given the conceptual rather than verbal link to 'Spirit of truth.'

echoes.text: But they rebelled, and grieved his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he himself fought against them. Then he remembered the days of old, Moses and his people, saying, Where is he who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? where is he who put his holy Spirit in their midst?
echoes.note: Israel 'grieved his Holy Spirit,' yet God 'put in the midst of them his Holy Spirit,' one of the rare OT uses of 'his Holy Spirit' that the Paraclete passages presuppose. The motif of God placing his Spirit among the people undergirds 14:16-17's abiding Counselor; medium for the shared 'Holy Spirit' terminology with the wider Isaianic-Spirit complex.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
echoes.note: 'I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh' is the eschatological Spirit-bestowal that 14:16-17 promises in personalized form as the indwelling Paraclete. Coherence is solid within John's realized-eschatology of the Spirit's coming; medium because John individualizes the corporate outpouring and offers no verbal quotation.

echoes.text: This is the word that I covenanted with you when you came out of Egypt, and my Spirit lived among you. ‘Don’t be afraid.’
echoes.note: 'My Spirit remains in your midst; do not fear' couples the abiding Spirit with the dismissal of fear, paralleling the Paraclete who abides 'forever' alongside 14:27's 'let not your heart be afraid.' Low confidence: a suggestive thematic pairing of abiding-Spirit and courage rather than a demonstrable citation.

echoes.text: Yahweh came down in the cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the Spirit that was on him, and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did so no more. But two men remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the Spirit rested on them; and they were of those who were written, but had not gone out to the Tent; and they prophesied in the camp. A young man ran, and told […]
echoes.note: The LORD takes the Spirit on Moses and places it on the seventy, with Moses wishing all the LORD's people were prophets endowed with the Spirit. This distribution of the Spirit to the community prefigures the Paraclete given to all the disciples; low and contested because the link is conceptual, lacking the 'Spirit of truth' vocabulary.

echoes.text: For a holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit. And will start away from thoughts that are without understanding, And will be put to confusion when unrighteousness has come in.
echoes.note: 'A holy and disciplined spirit will flee from deceit' and (1:7) 'the Spirit of the Lord has filled the world' offer a Second-Temple 'spirit of truth/wisdom that the deceitful world cannot hold,' resonant with 14:17's Spirit 'whom the world cannot receive.' Low confidence: deuterocanonical mood-music supporting the truth-vs-world contrast rather than a direct source.

echoes.text: You shall no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall your land any more be termed Desolate: but you shall be called Hephzibah, and your land Beulah; for Yahweh delights in you, and your land shall be married.
echoes.note: 'You shall no more be termed Forsaken (Azubah)... for the LORD delights in you' counters abandonment with renewed presence, faintly behind 'I will not leave you orphans (orphanous); I will come to you.' Low confidence: the not-forsaking promise is thematically apt but lacks the orphan lexeme; flagged contested as ambient consolation language.

echoes.text: Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or scared of them; for Yahweh your God himself is who goes with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you.”
echoes.note: 'He will not leave you or forsake you' is the classic divine-presence assurance, recast in 14:18 as Jesus' pledge not to abandon his own. The not-forsake formula gives modest Coherence with the consolation here; low because John uses the distinctive 'orphans' image rather than the Deuteronomic wording.

echoes.text: No man will be able to stand before you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you nor forsake you.
echoes.note: 'I will not leave you or forsake you,' God's commissioning promise to Joshua, contributes to the OT not-forsake topos standing behind 'I will not leave you orphans.' Recurrence of this formula (Deut/Josh) raises its cumulative Volume slightly, but the link to 14:18 remains thematic; low and contested.

echoes.text: A father of the fatherless, and a defender of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.
echoes.note: God as 'father of the fatherless (orphans)' supplies the one strong OT orphan-care motif behind Jesus' refusal to leave the disciples 'orphans.' Figural and contested: the shared orphan vocabulary is suggestive, but John applies it to bereaved disciples rather than to literal orphans, so the connection is allusive at best.

echoes.text: After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him. Let us acknowledge Yahweh. Let us press on to know Yahweh. As surely as the sun rises, Yahweh will appear. He will come to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.”
echoes.note: 'After two days he will revive us... that we may live before him,' a revival-after-a-little-while hope, lightly resonates with 14:19, 'because I live, you also will live,' and 'yet a little while.' Low confidence: the life-after-interval pattern is genuinely parallel but verbally diffuse, and the resurrection-on-the-third-day reading is contested.

registers.label: Spare
lines: I will not leave you orphaned, he said.
He is coming to us still.
The Father will send another Advocate,
the Spirit of truth, to be with us always.
In him we live and move and have our being.
We are never beyond his keeping.
Christ is risen!
Christ is risen, alleluia!

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Come, all you who have felt left behind, who know what an empty house can feel like; hear the promise — I will not leave you orphaned.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
He is sending another Advocate, the Spirit of truth, to live not far off but near, with you and in you.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
For in God we live and move and have our being; there is no road that runs past the edge of his love.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
So come and bless our God, you peoples; he has kept us among the living and held our feet from slipping.
Christ is risen, alleluia!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: I will not leave you orphaned, says the Lord.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
He sends the Spirit of truth to be with us always.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
In him we live and move and have our being.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
Bless our God, you peoples. Come, let us worship.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
